_status: NEW 2026-08-17. India's third slice, and the one that connects the Indian branch to the rest of the graph for the first time. After BRICS/G.2, India had fifteen corpus nodes and ZERO edges to any non-Indian node -- the largest fully disconnected island in the corpus. This round asks REPORTS.md's secondary-objective question of India: which supranational bodies issue a standard that an Indian statistic is documented as methodologically dependent on? Answer: five, across eight edges. THE MOST SATISFYING RESULT NEEDED NO NEW RESEARCH AT ALL -- `in-mospi-cpi`'s own release text, quoted in that node's description since BRICS/G.1, states verbatim that the series "is aligned with the United Nations' Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018". The edition is named, the citation is in the dependent document's own text, and the edge was available for two rounds without being drawn. It is drawn here, directly from the existing node. Five new Indian source nodes carry the rest: the MoSPI expert-group report defining the CPI 2024 series, the GDP base-revision sub-committee report that finally names SNA 2008 in current non-obsolete text, NIC 2025, the Ministry of Finance's external-debt status report, and the RBI's balance-of-payments methodology. An eighth edge runs from `in-fc15-report` to the IMF's World Economic Outlook, which matters structurally out of proportion to its strength: FC15 sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so that single citation is what attaches the Finance Commission cluster itself to the international layer. Refusals are recorded in `_dropped`, including one where a verified-looking result was rejected because the host could not be reached for raw verification.
_note: ACCESS AND VERIFICATION. Sources are TIER A -- plain curl, genuine HTTP 200, real document bytes on the issuing agency's own host -- with ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION described below. The Indian trust-store fixes from BRICS/G.2 were reused and confirmed: `dea.gov.in` chains to Let's Encrypt intermediate YR1, absent from the container store, fixed by fetching `http://yr1.i.lencr.org/`, converting DER to PEM and appending to the system bundle -- verified cleanly with no `-k`. `censusindia.gov.in` needs the eMudhra emSign intermediate the same way. The diagnostic trap from G.2 is restated because it is easy to fall into twice: running `openssl s_client` DIRECTLY shows the egress gateway's own certificate and verifies cleanly, which is misleading -- it must be run THROUGH the proxy to see the real upstream chain. `www.rbi.org.in` serves plain HTML fine; only `rbidocs.rbi.org.in` is behind the F5/Shape TSPD bot-wall, and `/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` remains impassable even with the cookie-plus-Referer method that works for `/rdocs/Publications/PDFs/`. `r.jina.ai` remains Cloudflare-403, so no TIER B fallback exists. THE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, recorded because it is a live application of this project's own hardest-won lesson: the GASAB standard IGFRS 1 contains what appears to be an excellent IPSAS dependency, but `gasab.gov.in` returns `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` on both the document and the site root, and 503 over plain HTTP. The research agent reached the content only through WebFetch, on a different egress. Since AF/G.24 established that WebFetch has fabricated plausible content for unreachable URLs, and since no independent raw verification was possible from here, THE EDGE IS NOT MINTED -- see `_dropped`. Every `basis` below is this session's own read of the underlying research; full research log in `BRICS/G.3-research/india.md`.

reports.title: Expert Group Report on Comprehensive Updation of Consumer Price Index
reports.publisher: Price Statistics Division, National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: The 258-page expert-group report, dated January 2026, that defines the methodology of India's CPI 2024=100 series -- and the document that ties India's CPI to two international instruments by name and edition. On classification, §3.3 (Summary of Key Recommendations): "To enhance credibility and to ensure global comparability of Indian CPI, the latest structure of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 will be adopted in the CPI 2024 series." Corroborated at §2.3: "CPI 2024 – The latest classification framework is COICOP 2018. The CPI 2024 series is mostly aligned with COICOP 2018 with 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Sub-classes." and at §4.1.5: "EG recommended for mapping HCES items as per COICOP 2018 in CPI 2024." On method, the IMF manual is used NORMATIVELY rather than decoratively -- §4.6.5: "The procedure is fully consistent with the principles of the IMF CPI Manual (2020) and supports a smooth, stable, and operationally feasible implementation of the chain-base CPI."; §5.3.2: "This is one of the three methods prescribed in the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods 2020 (page 35) in case, if the price of social security transfers decreases from some positive amount to zero."; and §5.4.2 quotes the manual's text directly: "In this regard, the IMF's CPI Manual Concepts and Methods 2020 para 2.60 may be seen below: 'The expenditure on social transfers in kind is incurred by the governments or nonprofit institutions that pay for them, and not by the households that consume them....'" The report also records the PREDECESSOR series' classification lineage -- §4.1.1: "In India, in the CPI (2012=100) series COICOP 1999 was adopted with some deviations" -- which is deliberately not turned into an edge; see `_dropped`. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 5.2MB PDF.
reports.cadence_note: A one-off expert-group report rather than a recurring release, qualifying as a standing instrument that defines a method -- it is the document that fixes the classification structure and index formulae of the CPI 2024=100 series. Comparable in role to `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915` on the Russian side, which is why the two are typed the same way.

reports.title: Report of the Sub-Committee for Incorporation of New Data Sources, Rates and Ratios — For base year revision of GDP (2011-12 to 2022-23)
reports.publisher: National Accounts Division, National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: The National Accounts Division's base-year-revision sub-committee report, constituted under the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS) and published on mospi.gov.in on 24 February 2026 -- and the document that resolves BRICS/G.2's open India question by naming the SNA edition in CURRENT, non-obsolete text. Chapter 2 opens: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." -- "NAD" being the National Accounts Division, the compiler of `in-mospi-nas`. This matters because G.2 had to refuse the NAS-to-SNA-2008 edge: the NAS publication's own press release says only "in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year, and the only documents naming "SNA 2008" were a FAQ and a 2015 methodology volume watermarked OBSOLETE. This report is neither -- it was checked for an OBSOLETE watermark and carries none. A FORWARD-LOOKING SIGNAL is recorded and deliberately NOT turned into an edge: §1.6 lists "v. Sub-Committee for SNA 2025 Update" among the five sub-committees constituted for the revision. That names an internal committee, not a published Indian statistic compiled on SNA 2025, so no `sna-2025` edge is drawn -- but when that sub-committee reports, the edge may become real. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 32MB PDF, re-verified with a range request.
reports.cadence_note: A one-off sub-committee report tied to a specific base-year revision, qualifying as a standing methodological instrument rather than a recurring release. India's GDP base-year revisions occur roughly once a decade, so a successor document is expected rather than scheduled.

reports.title: National Industrial Classification 2025 (NIC-2025)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: India's national industrial classification, published on mospi.gov.in on 18 November 2025, and an unusually clean instance of a national classification stating that its own structure IS the international one. Introduction: "The classification aligns with the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC Rev. 5) while addressing specific features of the Indian economy such as the informal sector, agriculture, renewable energy, and the growing digital economy." And under Salient Features: "Based on ISIC Rev. 5: NIC-2025 is aligned with the latest international standard, ISIC Revision 5, ensuring structural and conceptual comparability up to the 4-digit class level." The document also records the lineage of its predecessors in a table of national-versus-international versions -- "NIC 2008 | ISIC Rev 4 (2008) | Sections 21, Divisions 88, Groups 238, Classes 403, Sub-Classes 1304" -- and notes that "The Indian Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) fully adopted ISIC Rev.1 at the division level", so the dependency is a documented sixty-year pattern rather than a one-off alignment. A NODE-IDENTITY NOTE, checked before minting: the corpus's `isic` node is deliberately the unversioned FAMILY node ("the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications"), not a revision-specific node, so pointing an ISIC Rev. 5 citation at it raises no edition problem -- unlike SNA and COICOP, which the corpus does split by edition. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 5.1MB PDF.
reports.cadence_note: A standing classification, revised generationally rather than on a cadence -- SIC 1962, then NIC 2008, now NIC 2025, each tracking a successive ISIC revision.

reports.title: India's External Debt: A Status Report
reports.publisher: External Debt Management Unit, Economic Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
reports.description: The Ministry of Finance's annual external-debt status report -- the 2024-25 edition, September 2025, 114 pages -- and the best Indian-hosted, Indian-authored primary text naming the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard. Annex "II. Dissemination of External Debt Statistics in India" states: "India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund." and "The external debt statistics of India are disseminated with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter in both the country-specific and SDDS format and are accessible at www.finmin.nic.in and www.rbi.org.in." The report also names the IMF's External Debt Statistics Guide as its compilation basis -- Annex (vi): "The external debt statistics are compiled using the methodology and practices prescribed in the 'External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users' brought out by the IMF", with §2.15 confirming operative use: "the data on India's external debt is presented according to the IMF format (as per the IMF's 2013 EDS Guide format), classified by debtor sectors." That Guide has no corpus node yet; see `_dropped`, along with the reason its footnoted mentions of SNA 2008 and BPM6 are NOT turned into edges. Fetched TIER A from dea.gov.in once the Let's Encrypt YR1 intermediate was supplied to the trust bundle.
reports.cadence_note: Annual -- one status report per financial year, the verified instance being 2024-25 published September 2025. The underlying statistics are quarterly, disseminated "with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter" per the report's own Annex II.

reports.title: Developments in India's Balance of Payments (RBI Bulletin quarterly article and associated BoP statistics)
reports.description: The Reserve Bank's quarterly balance-of-payments publication, and a first-person statement that India's BoP is compiled and presented on BPM6. The article's opening paragraph: "The data on India's Balance of Payments (BoP) are compiled and published by the Reserve Bank on a quarterly basis with a lag of one quarter. The compilation of BoP data is based on the IMF guidelines set out in its Balance of Payments Manual (BPM) which is revised from time to time. IMF has recently brought out the Sixth Edition of BPM, i.e., BPM6 which has suggested revised compilation procedure as well as new format of standard presentation of BoP statistics. ... Accordingly, from this quarter (Q4 of 2010-11), BoP data are presented in the revised format as per BPM6." Annex 2 records the Indian decision instrument behind the switch: "The Report of the Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India (Chairman: Shri Deepak Mohanty), released by the RBI on its website ... on November 23, 2010, had recommended that the BoP data for India should be presented in the new format of standard presentation of BoP as suggested by the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual (Sixth Edition), i.e., BPM6." The statistical tables are themselves headed "Statement I: Standard Presentation of BoP as per BPM6 (US$ million)", with a table note reading "Changes in Reserve Assets are included under the Financial Account as recommended by the BPM 6." A DATING WEAKNESS is stated rather than hidden: the verified article is the Q4 2010-11 transition issue, so it documents ADOPTION rather than confirming present practice -- however every later RBI BoP statement is still headed "as per BPM6", and the Ministry of Finance's September 2025 external-debt report independently confirms BPM6 as the live framework. A current quarterly BoP press release would strengthen this; those live behind the `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` bot-wall that this round could not pass. Fetched TIER A as plain HTML from www.rbi.org.in.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, stated in the publication's own first sentence: "compiled and published by the Reserve Bank on a quarterly basis with a lag of one quarter."

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY from the node's OWN release document, and available since BRICS/G.1 without being drawn -- the single cheapest edge in this round. The July 2026 CPI press release, which is `in-mospi-cpi`'s own url, states verbatim: "The CPI (Base: 2024=100) series is aligned with the United Nations' Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018, comprising 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Subclasses." That sentence names the classification, its issuing body, AND the edition -- satisfying the edition rule outright, with no companion document required and no inference. It has been quoted in the `in-mospi-cpi` node description since G.1; what was missing was the edge, not the evidence. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: COICOP 2018 supplies the index's own classification structure down to the sub-class level, which is method, not reference. Corroborated independently by MoSPI's expert-group report (see the next edge). WEAKNESS STATED: the release says "aligned with", and the expert-group report elaborates that the series is "mostly aligned" -- India uses 12 Divisions against COICOP 2018's 15, with documented mapping compromises where household-survey items could not be mapped unambiguously. The dependency is real and named; the conformance is partial, and this corpus has no relationship type expressing partial conformance, so the qualification is recorded here.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named repeatedly. §3.3: "To enhance credibility and to ensure global comparability of Indian CPI, the latest structure of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 will be adopted in the CPI 2024 series." §2.3: "CPI 2024 – The latest classification framework is COICOP 2018. The CPI 2024 series is mostly aligned with COICOP 2018 with 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Sub-classes." §4.1.5: "EG recommended for mapping HCES items as per COICOP 2018 in CPI 2024." This is the methodology document that DECIDES the classification the CPI release then reports using, so the two edges into `un-coicop-2018` are complementary rather than duplicative -- one records what the published index is built on, the other records the instrument that chose it. `methodology_depends_on` on the same reasoning as the release-level edge.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, with the edition named and the manual applied NORMATIVELY rather than cited for colour -- it supplies the menu of options from which MoSPI picks its treatment. §4.6.5: "The procedure is fully consistent with the principles of the IMF CPI Manual (2020) and supports a smooth, stable, and operationally feasible implementation of the chain-base CPI." §5.3.2 and §5.3.4 go further and take a decision from it: "This is one of the three methods prescribed in the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods 2020 (page 35) in case, if the price of social security transfers decreases from some positive amount to zero." followed by the three methods and MoSPI's choice, "Method 1: To use a zero price and adjust the weight during next update. (Proposed for new series of CPI)". §5.4.2 quotes the manual's paragraph 2.60 verbatim. The full title and year are given, with page and paragraph references (p.35, paras 2.60, 2.72). NODE IDENTITY CHECKED before minting: the `cpi-manual` node's own description identifies it as the 2020 edition updating the 2004 ILO-managed predecessor, matching what the Indian document names -- had the node been the 2004 edition, the edition rule would have required refusing this edge. Note the pleasing symmetry with the Russian side of this round: `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915 -> cpi-manual` rests on the same manual, named with the same year, in a document of the same kind.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named, and it closes the question BRICS/G.2 had to leave open. Chapter 2's opening sentence: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." The edition is explicit, the compiler named is the National Accounts Division itself, and the claim is about how India's GDP estimates ARE compiled rather than how they might be. `methodology_depends_on`: "as per recommendations of" introduces the sectoral framework actually used. THE SCOPE LIMIT IS THE REASON THIS EDGE IS MINTED FROM A NEW NODE RATHER THAN FROM `in-mospi-nas`: the quote is from a companion methodology report of the National Accounts Division, not from the body of the National Accounts Statistics publication, whose own release text still says only "System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year. Attaching the edge to `in-mospi-nas` would put a citation in that node's mouth that its document does not make -- so the report is minted as its own node instead, exactly as the Russian side handles `ru-rosstat-osm-233-household-accounts`. Secondary corroboration in the same PDF (§1.1, "consistent with the System of National Accounts (SNA) guidelines") is unversioned and would not support an edge alone.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. NIC-2025's Introduction: "The classification aligns with the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC Rev. 5) while addressing specific features of the Indian economy such as the informal sector, agriculture, renewable energy, and the growing digital economy." And under Salient Features: "Based on ISIC Rev. 5: NIC-2025 is aligned with the latest international standard, ISIC Revision 5, ensuring structural and conceptual comparability up to the 4-digit class level." `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the national classification's structure IS the international one to four digits, which is as strong as a classification dependency gets. NODE-IDENTITY CHECK, and the reason no edition problem arises: the corpus's `isic` node is deliberately the unversioned FAMILY node -- its own description calls it "the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors" -- so it is designed to receive citations of any revision, unlike `sna-2008`/`sna-2025` and `un-coicop-2018`/`un-coicop-hbs-1999`, which are edition-split. Recorded because a future round may reasonably propose splitting `isic` by revision, at which point this edge would need re-pointing to a Rev. 5 node, and NIC 2008's separately documented dependency on ISIC Rev. 4 would become mintable as well.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, from an Indian-authored, Indian-hosted primary document -- which is what the evidence standard requires, an IMF-side claim of Indian coverage would not qualify. Annex II: "India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund." and, operatively: "The external debt statistics of India are disseminated with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter in both the country-specific and SDDS format and are accessible at www.finmin.nic.in and www.rbi.org.in." NO EDITION PROBLEM: SDDS is a single named standard rather than an edition series, and the Indian text names it by full title. `methodology_depends_on` because the standard governs the dissemination FORMAT and periodicity actually used -- the dependency is on SDDS's dissemination dimension, stated plainly here rather than implied to be broader.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, first-person and edition-named. "The compilation of BoP data is based on the IMF guidelines set out in its Balance of Payments Manual (BPM) ... IMF has recently brought out the Sixth Edition of BPM, i.e., BPM6 which has suggested revised compilation procedure as well as new format of standard presentation of BoP statistics. ... Accordingly, from this quarter (Q4 of 2010-11), BoP data are presented in the revised format as per BPM6." The RBI's own statistical tables carry it in their headings -- "Statement I: Standard Presentation of BoP as per BPM6 (US$ million)" -- and a table note reads "Changes in Reserve Assets are included under the Financial Account as recommended by the BPM 6." `methodology_depends_on`: BPM6 supplies both the compilation procedure and the presentation format of India's published BoP. TENSE WEAKNESS STATED HONESTLY, since this project's own spec insists on it: the verified article is the Q4 2010-11 transition issue, so its central sentence documents the moment of adoption. That is a PAST-tense event, and on its own would be exactly the kind of past arrangement this corpus refuses to treat as a live dependency. It is minted because two independent present-tense confirmations exist: the RBI's statistical statements are still headed "as per BPM6", and the Ministry of Finance's September 2025 external-debt report treats BPM6 as the current framework. A current RBI quarterly BoP press release would remove the caveat entirely and is a clean lead -- blocked only by the `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` bot-wall.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the most important edge in this file: `in-fc15-report` sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so this single citation is what attaches the whole Finance Commission cluster -- Constitution, Commission reports, Explanatory Memoranda, Union Budget, RBI State Finances, CAG -- to the international layer. FC15 Volume I cites the WEO in two footnotes supporting its macroeconomic narrative: "1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020" and "4 World Economic Outlook October 2020, International Monetary Fund". `uses_data_from` rather than `methodology_depends_on`, deliberately: the WEO supplies comparator data and growth figures the Commission reasons from; it is not a standard the Commission's methodology conforms to. ON THE EDITION QUESTION, which the research flagged and which is worth settling here as a corpus rule: `imf-weo` is NOT edition-split and should not be, because the WEO is a RECURRING PUBLICATION, not a standard with successor editions held as separate nodes. This corpus models a recurring release as one node covering all its issues -- `br-ipca` covers every month, `cn-nbs-statistical-communique` every year -- so citing the October 2020 issue is like citing a particular month of a monthly index, and points at the series node correctly. That is a different situation from SNA 2008 versus SNA 2025, which are successive STANDARDS deliberately held apart. WEAKNESS STATED: this is a footnote citation, the weakest form of dependency in this project's taxonomy. A third mention (the source line of Figure 2.2, "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook, and staff calculations") is unversioned and would not qualify alone.

_dropped.edge: in-gasab-igfrs-1 -> ipsas (GASAB's IGFRS 1 residual dependency on IPSAS)
_dropped.why: REFUSED FOR LACK OF RAW VERIFICATION, and recorded at length because it is a live application of this project's hardest-won methodological rule rather than a routine access failure. The apparent evidence is excellent: GASAB's *IGFRS 1 – Presentation of Financial Statements* reportedly states "Where relevant IGFRSs on specific accounting transactions are not available, the Government entity shall follow relevant International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), till an appropriate IGFRS is formulated" -- a RESIDUAL NORMATIVE dependency, which is the strongest possible form: IPSAS is the operative rule wherever no Indian standard exists. It also reportedly names IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 2 by number. THE PROBLEM: `gasab.gov.in` cannot be reached from this environment at all. Verified this session, twice, with a browser User-Agent: both `https://gasab.gov.in/gasab/pdf/IGFRS-1.pdf` and `https://gasab.gov.in/` return `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` (000/0), and plain HTTP returns 503. The content above was obtained by the research agent through WebFetch, on a different egress, and could not be independently confirmed. AF/G.24 established that WebFetch has FABRICATED plausible content for unreachable URLs rather than reporting failure, and this corpus's standing rule is to raw-verify before trusting any fetched quotation. The quotations may well be genuine -- they read entirely plausibly -- and that is precisely why the rule exists. NO EDGE, NO NODE. This is the highest-value single lead for a future round: one successful fetch of IGFRS 1 from a network that can reach gasab.gov.in mints a node and an edge, and connects India's public-sector accounting to the same `ipsas` node Brazil's `br-mcasp` already reaches.

REFUSED as transitive, on this project's own "comparable with is not a dependency" rule. Both editions ARE named, in one sentence, in a footnote to the external-debt report: "The concepts set out in the IMF's External Debt Statistics (EDS) Guide 2013 are harmonized with those of the System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 and the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6) published in 2009." But read carefully, that sentence asserts a property of the EDS GUIDE, not a dependency of India's statistics: it says the Guide is HARMONIZED WITH SNA 2008 and BPM6. India's own stated dependency, in Annex (vi), is on the Guide -- "compiled using the methodology and practices prescribed in the 'External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users' brought out by the IMF" -- so any dependency on SNA 2008 or BPM6 from this document is INDIRECT, running through the Guide. REPORTS.md states plainly that "comparable with"-type language is not a dependency, and "harmonized with" is the same shape. Minting these would also double-count: India's BPM6 dependency is separately and directly evidenced from the RBI, and is minted from there. The honest fix is to mint the EDS Guide as its own node and edge this report to it -- see the next entry.

_dropped.edge: in-mof-external-debt-status-report -> IMF External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users (2013)
_dropped.why: A fully evidenced, edition-named dependency on an international manual the corpus does not hold. §2.15 states operative use: "the data on India's external debt is presented according to the IMF format (as per the IMF's 2013 EDS Guide format), classified by debtor sectors", and a further footnote pins the same 2013 edition alongside BPM6. Target would be *External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users* (2013), IMF et al., `https://www.imf.org/external/np/sta/ed/guide.htm`. Would be `methodology_depends_on` at STRONG confidence. NOTE AN EDITION SUBTLETY for whoever mints it: the same Indian report ALSO cites the 2003 edition, for a different purpose -- the definition of external debt -- so two editions are in play in one document and a corpus that splits them will need both, exactly as it splits SNA. Note also that Annex (vi)'s statement gives the Guide's title UNVERSIONED; the 2013 year comes from §2.15 and the footnote, so the edge depends on reading the document as a whole.

STILL REFUSED at the NAS publication level, and the refusal is unchanged from BRICS/G.2 even though the SNA 2008 edge now exists elsewhere in the corpus. The NAS release's own text says only: "These estimates are presented at current and constant (2011-12) prices and are based on the methodologies in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)." -- no year. Under the edition rule that cannot select between `sna-2008` and `sna-2025`. What CHANGED this round is that a current, non-obsolete MoSPI document naming "System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008" was found and minted as `in-mospi-gdp-base-revision-2026`, so India's national accounts are now attached to SNA 2008 in the graph -- just not from this node, because this node's document does not say it. Recorded so a future session does not read the new edge and conclude the NAS-level one was an oversight.

_dropped.edge: in-mospi-cpi -> un-coicop-hbs-1999 (via the predecessor CPI 2012=100 series)
_dropped.why: REFUSED on two independent grounds, both worth recording. MoSPI's expert-group report does name an edition for the OLD series: "In India, in the CPI (2012=100) series COICOP 1999 was adopted with some deviations to classify the items into different groups, subgroups and sections", and "The series was partially aligned with UNSD endorsed classification system i.e. Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 1999." GROUND ONE: the dependent is the CPI 2012=100 series, which the corpus does not hold -- `in-mospi-cpi` is the 2024=100 series, a different index with a different classification, so attaching this to it would be a wrong-target error. GROUND TWO: the Indian text says plain "COICOP 1999" (UNSD), whereas the corpus node id `un-coicop-hbs-1999` reads as the *Household Budget Surveys* variant -- these may be different publications, and that identity question should be settled before any edge is drawn to that node from anywhere. The relationship is also expressly superseded. If a future round wants an `in-mospi-cpi-2012` node, this is a ready edge subject to ground two.

NOT FOUND for the specific existing nodes. The State Finances Audit Report does not name IPSAS, nor ISSAI 300 (Performance Audit Principles) or ISSAI 400 (Compliance Audit Principles) -- the two INTOSAI nodes the corpus happens to hold. Separately, CAG's *Auditing Standards 2017* WERE found to cite INTOSAI's ISSAI framework, but not those two instruments, so forcing that citation onto `intosai-issai-300`/`intosai-issai-400` would be a wrong-target error of the same kind refused for the ICLS resolution on the Russian side of this round. Minting CAG's Auditing Standards as a node, together with whichever ISSAIs it actually names, is a clean and well-scoped lead for a future round -- and would give India's audit tier an international attachment matching the one Brazil's `br-mcasp -> ipsas` already provides.

NOT FOUND, and a genuine surprise worth recording rather than passing over. The UN's *Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses* is the obvious international standard for a national census, the corpus already holds it as `un-census-principles`, and India's census is among the largest statistical operations in the world -- yet no reachable Census of India document naming it was located this round. This may well be a search limitation rather than an absence: census methodology is spread across administrative manuals and instruction booklets rather than a single methodology volume, and `censusindia.gov.in` required a trust-store fix to reach at all. Recorded as an open lead rather than a settled negative.

NOT FOUND. India's Union Budget documents do not name GFSM 2014, IPSAS or the SNA. The Indian government-finance-statistics dependency, if one is documented anywhere, is more likely to sit with the Controller General of Accounts or GASAB than in the Budget itself.

UNRESOLVED rather than NOT FOUND -- the distinction matters. The RBI publication landing page resolves (HTTP 200, foreword text confirmed present) but the report PDF links are injected client-side and resolve to `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/Publications/PDFs/...`, which this round could not enumerate from the returned HTML. _dropped.edge: PEFA Framework for assessing public financial management (2016), and the RBI Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India (2010), as nodes
_dropped.why: Two further named instruments surfaced this round with no corpus node. (1) FC15 Volume I cites the PEFA Framework with a full methodological description -- "PEFA is a methodology for assessing public financial management performance. It identifies ninety-four characteristics (dimensions) across thirty-one key components of public financial management (indicators) in seven broad areas of activity (pillars)." PEFA is a real international assessment framework and the corpus already holds one PEFA-derived African document (`bf-pefa-ouagadougou-2021`), so a PEFA Framework node would serve more than one branch. (2) The *Report of the Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India* (Chairman: Deepak Mohanty), RBI, released 23 November 2010, is the Indian instrument that DECIDED the BPM6 adoption and would be the cleanest possible source node for an `-> imf-bpm6` edge -- better than the transition-quarter bulletin article minted here, because it is a standing decision document rather than a dated news item. It was named but not retrieved this round.
